title: Acme Wallet onboarding: two defects on the connect step
subtitle: Synthetic worked example for `bin/fm-visual-findings.sh`. The screenshot is a mock page, and every file path below is invented.
meta: commit `0000000` (main) · mock build · captured at a 500x844 viewport

findings.title: The connect screen tells the user to tap a button that does not exist
findings.summary: The paragraph names a **“Proceed to scan”** button. The only button on the screen says **“Get connected”**, and no locale file defines that other label at all.
findings.alt: The Acme Wallet connect screen, with the instruction paragraph and the primary button ringed
findings.caption: Coordinates came straight from `getBoundingClientRect()` at a 500x844 viewport, which is also the screenshot's pixel size, so no coordinate space had to be declared.

evidence.heading: the instruction
evidence.note: The onboarding copy sends the user looking for a button by name.
evidence.code:
"instruction": "If you are ready and understand, tap the
  “Proceed to scan” button. That opens a scanner
  where you scan the QR code or enter the URL by hand."

evidence.heading: the actual button
evidence.note: Two keys further down the same file, the button is called something else. The label has no branch on connection state, so this is what *every* user sees.

evidence.heading: and nothing else defines the other label

body.code:
src/locales/en/connect.json:41:  "instruction": "... tap the “Proceed to scan” button ..."
(1 match, in prose only)
body.caption: grep -rn "Proceed to scan" src/locales/

body.text: **“Proceed to scan” appears in no button key, in any locale file.** It reads as a rename that left the paragraph behind.

findings.verdict: Real but cosmetic, and the kind of thing that may already be known upstream. Worth a one-line copy fix, not worth blocking a release.

findings.title: Both connect-step inputs ship the same test id
findings.summary: Nothing is visibly wrong on screen, which is exactly why this needs the code rather than a screenshot: the selector resolves to two elements and every assertion silently reads the first one.

body.code:
<Input data-testid="connect-url-input" value={url} onChange={setUrl} />
<Input data-testid="connect-url-input" value={alias} onChange={setAlias} />

body.text: Both fields were copied from the same block and kept the same identifier. Two things follow:

bullets: **`getByTestId` throws** on multiple matches, so the selector is unusable as written.
**`getAllByTestId` silently succeeds**, which is what the existing test does, so the hole stays invisible.

evidence.heading: what the test then proves
evidence.note: The assertion takes index 0, so the alias field is never exercised and a regression in it cannot fail this suite.

findings.verdict: Substantive: it is a hole in the test suite rather than a visible bug, so it will not surface on its own until something breaks in the untested field.
